record.what_it_does: Clay is a GTM (go-to-market) data platform that lets users search a proprietary companies/people database, enrich records via 150+ third-party data providers and AI research agents ("Claygents"), and run automated prospecting workflows.
record.auth_notes: The Public API (REST) uses a static personal API key sent in a `clay-api-key` header, created under Settings → Account → API keys (beta) in the Clay app — this is a Bearer/API-key style credential, not an OAuth flow, and is tied to one Clay user/workspace. Separately, Clay's MCP server (https://api.clay.com/v3/mcp) uses full OAuth2 with Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591), PKCE, and per-user/per-workspace authorization codes — this is the method a multi-tenant agent toolkit would use since each end user authorizes their own workspace via a standard OAuth consent screen.
record.access_notes: Clay's Free plan gives immediate API-key and MCP access with no cost. The developer docs state 'The developer platform is available across all Clay plans, including free and trial plans,' though usage is capped on Free (e.g. 100 data credits/mo, 500 actions/mo, search results limited to 50/request and 100/mo). The `Tables` API primitive specifically requires an Enterprise plan; Search and Routines (the core primitives) work on all plans including Free.
record.main_blocker: Narrow/moderate REST surface (search, routines/functions, tables, me — roughly a dozen documented endpoints) with the richest data primitive (Tables) gated to Enterprise plans; some endpoints are async/polling-based.

evidence.quote: Every request to the Clay Public API must include a Clay API key in the `clay-api-key` header.

record.open_questions: Exact total endpoint count wasn't independently tallied beyond the ~12 listed in llms.txt (search, routines, tables, me + variants), so api_breadth is an estimate of 'moderate' rather than a precise count; it may read as 'narrow' depending on threshold. Rate limits and full error taxonomy were not individually verified.
